title: byte, int, uint8_t, and fixed-width types

spans.text: Arduino `byte` is an alias for an unsigned 8-bit value from 0 to 255; `uint8_t` is explicitly 8 bits. `int` varies by board: often 16 bits on classic UNO and 32 bits on ESP32. Use `uint8_t` for protocol bytes, `uint32_t` for large counters, and `size_t` for sizes and indexes.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Unsigned types cannot represent negative values and wrap on overflow. `float` precision and ADC ranges vary by platform. Check valid ranges and `sizeof(type)`.
